page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton2 processors. The system delivers 32 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 12 Gbps. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the m6gd.8xlarge consistently in the middle tier for multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,563.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,587.0, aided by software compilation scores of 25,266.0. Memory throughput reaches 166.08 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 75.41 GB/sec for write operations. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register lower, with a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0, single-thread gzip compression at 20.31 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 7.38 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 1900 GB direct-attached NVMe SSD storage combined with 32 dedicated physical ARM cores provides high architectural efficiency for IOPS-intensive workflows. The hardware configuration demonstrates strong throughput in structured workloads, handling 36.57 million Redis SET operations per second and 33.39 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Small model LLM text generation is constrained, achieving 39.3 tokens per second, but 7B model text generation reaches an expected 15.1 tokens per second. The instance provides balanced throughput across multi-threaded applications, making it well suited for distributed relational databases, caching layers, containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM-based instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz with dedicated single-threaded cores. The hardware configuration features 128.0 GB of RAM, 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation displays balanced multi-core and memory throughput, yielding 48,563.19 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 36.57 million Redis SET operations per second, and 33.39 GB/sec in static web serving. While single-thread instruction throughput is modest compared to alternative architectures, its local high-speed NVMe storage and dedicated core footprint provide reliable density for high-throughput applications. It is appropriate for containerized backend services, caching clusters, compilation farms, and localized database workloads.
